candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — communication, client rights, incident response and quality/safety
candidate.educational_objective: Apply AHRQ CANDOR principles for transparent, compassionate communication after a harmful adverse event.

options.A: Delay disclosure until litigation is resolved and all uncertainty has disappeared.
options.B: Explain the known facts honestly without speculation, respond with empathy, and outline next steps and follow-up.
options.C: Avoid expressions of concern or apology because they always establish legal liability.
options.D: Have one unprepared clinician conduct the disclosure without team preparation or organizational support.

candidate.rationale: AHRQ CANDOR guidance recommends timely, honest and compassionate disclosure. The team should prepare for the conversation, explain known facts without speculation, listen and respond empathically, apologize appropriately, and describe next steps and follow-up. Therefore B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CANDOR disclosure includes team preparation, honest explanation of known facts without speculation, empathic listening, appropriate apology, discussion of next steps and follow-up, and documentation.
candidate.source_locator: Disclosure Checklist — Part II: Get Ready; Listen and Empathize Throughout; Explain the Facts; Apologize; Close the Discussion
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)

candidate.stem: After an adverse event that harmed a client, the care team prepares for disclosure to the client and family. Which approach best reflects AHRQ CANDOR guidance?
